text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: inference-queue-backlog fired (sev: high) for service `inference-hosting-prod` — 3xx backlog, latency rising. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

pagerduty: Page #1 -> oncall-alex (rotation)

oncall-alex: acked :white_check_mark:

oncall-alex: Seeing queue length spike on dispatcher. Alert shows queue depth ~18k and growing, worker pod CPU is ~40% tho.

sre-maya: that suggests warmup / cold-start or KV cache miss, not raw CPU saturation. Any node provisioning events?

infra-jess: checking cloud console — node launches delayed, ~7 nodes in provisioning state for 4m. provider reports warm pool depletion.

eng-sam: logs from dispatcher: `ERROR: task dequeue timeout after 30s` repeated. Also lots of 429 from backend model variant `v2-quant` around the same time.

oncall-alex: grabbing recent metrics: `inference.dispatcher.queue_length` timeline: 15k -> 20k over 6m. `worker.process_time.p95` went 220ms -> 2.3s. Error rate 0.8% -> 5% in last 10m. Customer-facing errors: increased timeouts.

sre-maya: autoscaler HPA target is `queue_length_per_pod` computed from a custom metric. suspicious: metric ingestion shows 2m lag in metrics-server. If HPA reads stale low values, it won't scale. Can someone check metric ingestion pipeline?

infra-jess: metrics-agent logs show spike in scrape latency and backlog on pushgateway — disk IO contention on metrics node. I'm promoting a metrics-agent to new instance.

eng-sam: meanwhile can we manually scale to drain queue? Suggest `kubectl scale deployment inference-worker --replicas=40 -n production` and then increase dispatcher concurrency.

oncall-alex: running manual scale now.

oncall-alex: `kubectl scale` returned success. Waiting for pods.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: 10 new pods started (inference-worker) — rolling up.

infra-jess: nodes coming up slowly, cloud provider is throttling new spot instances. Spinning some on-demand to bridge.

eng-sam: also toggled routing to fallback model `v1-small` for non-critical traffic to reduce pressure on heavy variant. Patch in feature flag: `routes.heavy -> fallback=true`

product-ops: any immediate customer impact notes? ETA to clear backlog?

oncall-alex: estimate: if new pods stabilize and KV caches warm, backlog should drain in ~8-12m. Current customer-visible: increased 95p latency and ~3-5% timed-out requests for some customers. Will notify support to open incident banner.

sre-maya: verified metric ingestion fix applied; HPA should now see real queue length. Recommend adding a short-term aggressive scale policy while we investigate root cause.

infra-jess: on-demand nodes up, pods initializing. Observed `kvcache.warmup.miss` spike in logs — warmup traffic needed.

eng-sam: running a synthetic warmup job to prefill KV caches: `kubectl run kv-warmup --image=tooling/warmup:latest --restart=OnFailure --replicas=50` — warming prefix sets.

oncall-alex: queue length starting to fall 20k -> 9k -> 3k in last 10m. p95 latency trending down to ~400ms. Error rate back toward baseline.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged and assigned to SRE rotation. Escalation not yet required.

product-ops: drafting customer note: "We saw elevated latency and transient timeouts between 14:03–14:20 UTC due to delayed autoscaling and cache warmup. Mitigation applied and traffic rerouted; ongoing monitoring."

eng-sam: temporary remediations applied: manual scale, on-demand nodes, fallback routing, synthetic warmups. Next: root-cause triage — metrics ingestion lag + provider warm pool exhaustion + no warmup guard in autoscaler.

sre-maya: handing off to infra-jess and eng-sam for follow-up. oncall-alex will remain watch for 30m.

oncall-alex: handing off — I'm stepping out for 20m but will stay available by DM. Please @mention me for any PD escalation.

infra-jess: action items created:
- increase metrics-agent resilience and add disk IO alert (infra-234)
- add HPA fallback rule to react to rapid queue growth even if metrics are delayed (infra-235)
- add synthetic warmup on scale-up events (eng-411)
- add PD rule to page when queue_length > 10k and p95 > 1s for >5m (slo-78)

eng-sam: will file a short postmortem and include tests to simulate provider warm pool depletion.

sre-maya: closing loop: queue drained to <200 in last 2m, latency back to normal for most customers. Marking incident as mitigated.

oncall-alex: thanks team. We'll keep the PD incident open until follow-ups are scheduled. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated — will auto-close PD after 1h if no regressions.

product-ops: will send customer-facing status update in 15m and coordinate with support.

eng-sam: quick note for post-incident: consider metric fallbacks that use dispatcher queue length from Redis directly if metrics-server lag detected.

sre-maya: acknowledged, assigned to triage board.

oncall-alex: end of thread for handoff."
